look_here_first: Start with WOODY branches, then inspect one OPPOSITE pair of oval/elliptic (sometimes obovate) leaves. Autumn sage has relatively smooth/glabrous blades with tiny pitted glands, and larger showy two-lipped red-pink (or other cultivar-color) flowers around 25 mm long in the UT Texas treatment. Shrubby blue sage can have similarly sized leaves, but leaf surfaces are rough/hairy and its blue-purple corollas are usually smaller (often <13 mm). Flower color alone is NOT enough, especially in cultivated salvias.
project_tracker_diagnostic: woody perennial subshrub/shrub; small aromatic elliptic to obovate leaves; often evergreen or tardily deciduous; showy relatively large flowers with strong color variation; dry rocky western Edwards Plateau/Trans-Pecos habitat

project_inclusion.range_basis: Bandera — NPSOT states the wild Texas range begins in western Bandera County and extends westward. Edwards — a documented NPSOT photo-contest field record places wild Salvia greggii at Kickapoo Caverns State Park, Edwards County. Kew confirms Texas as native, but a third explicit project-target county native occurrence has not yet been documented to the project standard.

morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey's landscaping frame reinforces the mounded woody-shrub habit and flowering architecture. A second desert-field video shows a mature calyx during seed collection, adding a useful fruiting-stage cue beyond the showy corolla.
morphology_keys.leaf_dimensions: UT Austin regional S. greggii blades ~8–48 × 3–22 mm, ovate/elliptic or oblanceolate with low scallops; overlaps S. ballotiflora leaf SIZE. Better check hair/texture plus the corolla.
morphology_keys.leaf_surface: Leaf blades generally not coarsely hairy, minutely gland-dotted/pitted; leaf can feel smooth compared with shrubby blue sage's conspicuous rough leaf hairs. Pitted glands require true macro.
morphology_keys.corolla: In UT Austin regional description, two-lipped corolla ~25 mm long, typically scarlet/rose-red wild; cultivated varieties can be white, orange, pink and purple. Do not use garden flower color as a wild-species diagnostic.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Terminal raceme with successive opposite pairs of ascending flowers, conspicuous comparatively large two-lipped lips and persistent glandular calyx.
morphology_keys.cultivar_caution: S. greggii is sold in many colors and can be confused in gardens with S. microphylla and Salvia × jamensis hybrids; cultivar or hybrid flowers do NOT confirm wild S. greggii identity or native provenance.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Salvia ballotiflora: S. greggii has larger showier flowers and generally larger less-hairy leaves; S. ballotiflora has tiny blue-purple flowers and small hairy rough leaves.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.look_here_first: Both are WOODY shrubs. Check a whole leaf and the FLOWER SIZE: Greggii smooth-ish oval leaves and large showy ~25-mm corollas; ballotiflora rough/hairy serrate leaves and smaller blue-purple ~10–13-mm corollas.

key.greggii: Many branched stems, often older brown woody lower portion
key.ballotiflora: Also woody and shrubby — not a decisive difference

key.greggii: Generally smooth to touch with minutely sunken gland dots, usually not conspicuously hirsute
key.ballotiflora: Conspicuous rough/hairy texture with small raised hairs both sides
key.photo_need: matched dorsal/abaxial leaf macros; scales and focus

key.greggii: Elliptic/obovate, often entire to low-crenate; 8–48 mm
key.ballotiflora: Ovate, serrated/wavy, about 15–38 mm; size overlaps
key.photo_need: whole leaf beside ruler, do not overstate width split

key.greggii: Conspicuous showy lip, about 25 mm long in regional treatment; color variable cultivars
key.ballotiflora: Smaller blue/lavender purple often less than 13 mm, multiple clustered
key.photo_need: side-on flower in millimeters for BOTH species

key.greggii: Short glandular hairs, ribs visible; needs macro
key.ballotiflora: Hairy calyx and tubular flower; also needs macro

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: GREGGII = smooth-ish leaf and BIG showy flower. BALLOTIFLORA = ROUGH leaf and SMALL blue-purple flower.
warnings: Leaf sizes overlap, and both are woody. Don't diagnose from shrub form alone.
S. greggii garden plants may be cultivars or hybrid S. × jamensis or S. microphylla lookalikes.
No invented gland arrows in ordinary habit photos.
